draft.title: Urban growth
card: Urban growth is an increase in the number of people living in towns and cities. It can also mean the built-up area of a city getting bigger.
births are greater than deaths in a city. The population rises without anyone moving in.
people move into a city from rural areas or from other countries. They often come for jobs, education or services.
A growing city can spread outwards, taking up more land at its edges. It can also grow upwards, with taller buildings that fit more people on the same land.
draft.remember: Cities grow when births exceed deaths or when people move in, and they spread outwards or upwards.

a.q: In one year, a city has 30,000 births and 12,000 deaths. What does this show?
opts: Growth through migration from rural areas
a.why: More births than deaths means the population rises through natural increase. The numbers say nothing about people moving in, so migration is not the answer. Taller buildings describe how a city spreads, not why its population rises.
a.clue: Look at births and deaths, not at people arriving.

b.q: Farm incomes fall in a region of Indonesia, and many young adults move to Jakarta to find work. Which type of urban growth does this describe?
b.why: People are moving from the countryside into the city, so this is migration from rural areas. It is not overseas migration, because they stay within Indonesia. Their children may later add to natural increase, but the move itself is migration.
b.clue: Where did the new residents come from?

problems.detail: The clue ('Look at births and deaths, not at people arriving') rules out both migration options, leaving only natural increase against an obviously unrelated building option. Students can answer without understanding the idea, and the question is very easy for Year 12 HSC.

proposal.title: Urban growth
card: Urban growth is a rise in the number of people living in a city, or the spread of its built-up area. Population growth = natural increase + net migration.
births minus deaths in a city. When births are greater, the population rises without anyone moving in.
people move into a city from rural areas or from other countries, often for jobs, education or services. Net migration is arrivals minus departures.
A growing city can spread outwards, taking up more land at its edges. It can also grow upwards, with taller buildings that fit more people on the same land.
proposal.remember: A city's population grows through natural increase plus net migration, and the city can spread outwards or upwards.

a.q: A city's population rises by 40,000 in a year. It has 30,000 births and 12,000 deaths. How did the rest of the growth happen?
a.why: Natural increase is 30,000 minus 12,000, which is 18,000. Growth was 40,000, so the other 22,000 came from net migration. The figure of 18,000 is the natural increase itself, not the migration part.
a.clue: Work out births minus deaths first, then compare it with the total.

b.q: Farm incomes fall in a region of Indonesia, and many young adults move to Jakarta to find work. Which type of urban growth does this describe?
b.why: People are moving from the countryside into the city, so this is migration from rural areas. It is not overseas migration, because they stay within Indonesia. Their children may later add to natural increase, but the move itself is migration.
b.clue: Where did the new residents come from?
